# Troubleshooting

Use when an iOS build, test, package resolution, or generated-code step fails.
## Common Pitfalls

### Never Edit Generated Files

Files marked `Generated by typeshare` will be overwritten on the next `just generate`. Add Swift extensions in separate files under `Extensions/` directories instead.

### Xcode Build Cache Stale After Core Changes

After changing `core/` and regenerating, Xcode may use stale cached artifacts. Run a clean build:
```bash
just clean
just build
```

### BsvHomeCore Rust Library Link Failures

If SwiftPM cannot resolve `BsvHomeCore` in a fresh checkout, or the build fails with missing `libbsv_home_core.a` or undefined `ffi_bsv_home_core_*` symbols:
```bash
just bootstrap
just build
```
`just bootstrap` creates the local UniFFI Swift/header sources and iOS Rust static libraries needed by SwiftPM and Xcode. From the repo root, use `just generate-core`, then `just run-ios`. The optional `BsvHomeWithCore` Xcode scheme combines cached BsvHomeCore generation with the normal app build.

### Multiple Simulators Match the Destination

`xcodebuild` fails with "multiple devices matched the request" when several simulators share the default name. Pass the exact device, in a worktree slot the slot's own simulator:
```bash
SIMULATOR_NAME=wt1 just build-for-testing
```

### Test Failures After Model Changes

When Core model changes break tests, regenerate first, then distinguish stale output, a regression, and an intentionally changed contract. Update expectations only when the intended contract requires it:
```bash
just generate
just test
```
Do not patch generated files to make tests pass.

## Common Recovery Commands

### Simulator Console Capture

Keep the reader for `simctl launch --console` or `--console-pty` alive until the app exits. Stopping only the console collector can leave an unread output FIFO: synchronous Rust tracing then blocks in `StdoutLock::write_all`, and other service futures wait on `Stdout.lock` even after their HTTP requests finish. Stop the diagnostic app before closing the collector, then relaunch with `--stdout=/dev/null --stderr=/dev/null` when console output is unnecessary. Collect only approved non-secret fields; never retain credentials, request headers, recovery material, or signing payloads in diagnostic output.

### Build Failures

```bash
just clean
just bootstrap
just build
```

Build logs live under `build/DerivedData`.

### Swift Package Resolution Issues

When package resolution hangs or fails after branch switches or submodule updates:
```bash
just spm-resolve
just spm-resolve-all
```
If still stuck, clear DerivedData: `just clean`, then `just bootstrap`.

### Failing Tests

- Re-run the narrowest relevant target with `just test <TARGET>`
- Use Xcode directly when you need interactive debugging for test failures

### Core and Generated Code Issues

```bash
just generate
just generate-core
```

The optional `BsvHomeWithCore` Xcode scheme can be used when you want generation and app build in one Xcode action.

Read `core/AGENTS.md` when the failure is caused by shared Rust or generated-model changes.

### Submodule Issues

```bash
cd ..
just setup-git
```

Use the repo root `just setup-git` command so submodule sync and recursive setup stay aligned with the monorepo workflow.

## Useful Paths

- `BsvHome.xcodeproj`
- `build/DerivedData`
- `Packages/Localization/`
- `scripts/generate-core.sh`

## Build Notes

- `just build` already uses `xcodebuild` internally
- If command-line iteration is blocked, use Xcode directly for build and debugger context
